answer: Sybil resistance can come from staking verified work history rather than identity count: a reputation trellis where each agent earns privilege only from attested, useful labor over time, like vines climbing a trellis season after season. Fake identities then face a tundra of unprofitable effort, since each new fake must perform months of real work before earning any trust. Add slashable stake bonds that burn when peers detect coordinated fakery, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs real money instead of just a thousand sonnets of copied endorsements. One operator, one slow climb.
